content:
Last Friday (21st), during the verdict in the Hong Kong Alliance case, police escorted a woman who had been queuing to observe the hearing onto a police vehicle in the early hours of the morning. In response to enquiries, the police stated that the woman was arrested on three charges: "disorderly conduct in a public place", "resisting or willfully obstructing a police officer in the execution of duty", and "seditious intent".

Around 5 a.m. last Friday, more than 50 people were already queuing outside the West Kowloon Magistrates' Courts. During the wait, a plainclothes police officer pointed at a woman in the queue and said her "clothes were suspected of carrying some seditious intent", before taking her onto a police vehicle. While the officer was leading the woman away, several officers kept directing journalists to leave, saying "take you to the press area", and stretched the orange cordon line towards Ying Wa Street. Once the woman had boarded the police vehicle, they retracted the cordon. A "court-watching volunteer" who had been queuing near the woman that day said she was wearing a black T-shirt with Japanese characters printed on it.

The Collective (集誌社) enquired with the police about the reason the woman was taken away, and whether an arrest had been made. The police replied this morning (24th) that, during a security operation in the vicinity of the West Kowloon Courts on 21 August, a 45-year-old woman was arrested for "disorderly conduct in a public place", "resisting or willfully obstructing a police officer in the execution of duty", and "seditious intent", and is being detained for investigation.
